haiku-low.q1: Gateway returns 401 and stops. The counter store is not touched, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: 100 per minute in total for Standard, since all of a customer's keys share one counter. Across a minute boundary, about 200.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After in seconds. The request is not forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A 429-rejected request is not counted and the counter does not change.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. It passed the check, so it was counted. The budget is not refunded.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request with no X-RateLimit-* headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED as a number; it is OPEN, so no limit is applied until product decides.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, per-customer keys rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Redis deletes each key 120 seconds after its first increment.
haiku-low.q9: Each minute has a new counter starting at zero. Old counters expire after 120 seconds. Nothing else is described.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Redis Lua script, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After = max(1, ceil(windowEnd - now)) seconds, where windowEnd = (floor(now/60)+1)*60, using the gateway clock.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retry; the document describes no store retry. The client gets the forwarded response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized and processing stops. No counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: 100 requests per minute total on Standard, since all of a customer's keys share one counter. (Enterprise limit is OPEN.)
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds). The backend never sees it; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The counter does not change on a denied request.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was a counted request, there is no refund, and the client gets the backend's 500 with rate-limit headers.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request with no X-RateLimit-* headers. The request may or may not have been counted.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: OPEN, not yet decided by product; no limit is applied and nothing ships for it until decided.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, in the key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. Redis expiry removes old counts: EXPIRE of 120 s is set when the first request in the window creates the key.
sonnet.q9: Each clock minute window has its own counter keyed by windowStart, so a new window starts with a fresh count of 0 at the next minute boundary. The old key expires 120 s after creation.
sonnet.q10: The check script does the read-compare-increment as one atomic step in Redis, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After = max(1, ceil(windowEnd - now)) seconds, where windowEnd = (floor(now/60)+1)*60, both from the gateway clock.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store; the document describes no retry. The client gets the response with no rate-limit headers (no X-RateLimit-*).
